editorial:
Imagine you are starting your dream job at a fancy research center, but instead of making scientific breakthroughs, you find your friends turning into fish. That is exactly what happens to Mari in this wild ride. She is a smart student trying to make her family proud, but the vibe at the Pacific Institute turns creepy fast. When her friend Nanako shows up dead and covered in scales, you realize this isn't just a biology project gone wrong. It is a fight for survival against something from the deep ocean that is tired of humans taking everything from the sea.

You will love the gross-out effects and the way the tension builds up as the team gets picked off one by one. While some of the acting feels a bit stiff, the shock value makes up for it. If you like movies where humans become the prey, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the reveal that an ancient sea curse is turning people into fish-human hybrids. Mari discovers that the experiments at the institute actually woke up this evil force. In the final scenes, the transformation becomes unstoppable, and the survivors realize that humanity is being replaced. The twist is that the ocean is reclaiming the land, leaving the characters as mutated monsters in a watery world where humans are now the food.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird Japanese horror and creature features.
